turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict each
candidate's largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, then select the 5
candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20 pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
To predict the largest second-harmonic generation (SHG) tensor component $|d_{ij}|$ for the given candidates and select the ones closest to 20 pm/V, we can analyze the chemical formulas and crystal structures of the provided materials. The dataset contains several known classes of infrared (IR) nonlinear optical (NLO) materials, many of which are recently discovered chalcogenides. 

Let's evaluate the expected SHG responses of the key NLO candidates in the pool based on structure-property relationships and literature benchmarks (often compared to the benchmark material $\text{AgGaS}_2$ (AGS), which has $d_{36} \approx 13.5$ pm/V):

1. **$\text{CdSiP}_2$ (c030):** A well-known chalcopyrite IR NLO material. It has a highly polarizable $d^{10}$ $\text{Cd}^{2+}$ cation and covalent Si-P bonds, leading to a very large SHG response of $d_{36} \approx 84$ pm/V. This is far above our target.
2. **$\text{AlGaAs}_2$ / $\text{Al}_3\text{Ga}_3\text{As}_6$ (c055):** Zinc-blende derivative III-V semiconductors have extremely large SHG responses, typically $|d_{ij}| > 100$ pm/V.
3. **$\text{Li}_2\text{SnSe}_3$ (c092):** This material features highly polarizable $\text{SnSe}_4$ tetrahedra. It is known to exhibit a large SHG response of approximately $2.5 \times \text{AGS}$, which translates to $\sim 34$ pm/V.
4. **$\text{Li}_2\text{MgGa}_2\text{Se}_5$ (c094–c099):** This quaternary chalcogenide incorporates alkaline and alkaline-earth metals to widen the bandgap. The $d^0$ $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ cation dilutes the NLO response slightly compared to transition metals, yielding an SHG response of $\sim 1.2 \times \text{AGS}$, which is $\approx 16$ pm/V.
5. **$\text{Li}_3\text{Mg}_2\text{Ga}_3\text{Se}_8$ (c014–c015):** Similar to the above, this compound exhibits an SHG response of $\sim 1.3 \times \text{AGS}$, which is $\approx 17.5$ pm/V.
6. **$\text{Li}_2\text{ZnGa}_2\text{Se}_5$ (c008–c013):** By replacing the $d^0$ $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ with a $d^{10}$ $\text{Zn}^{2+}$ cation, the covalency of the M-Se bonds increases, which enhances the optical nonlinearity. Literature reports show that $\text{Li}_2\text{ZnGa}_2\text{Se}_5$ achieves an excellent balance between a high laser damage threshold and a large SHG response of exactly **$\sim 1.5 \times \text{AGS}$**. Calculating this gives $1.5 \times 13.5 \text{ pm/V} = \mathbf{20.25 \text{ pm/V}}$. 

The $\text{Li}_2\text{ZnGa}_2\text{Se}_5$ candidates perfectly match the target value of 20 pm/V. The dataset contains multiple structural configurations/polymorphs for this exact stoichiometry (c008 through c013). We will select the first five of these entries.

Final: c008, c009, c010, c011, c012
